core_obligations: Reformulate the statement as a rule on the category $\mathcal{C}$ of locally quasi-finite syntomic morphisms whose morphisms $b/a$ induce an isomorphism of $Y'$ with an open subscheme of $X' \times_X Y$, requiring compatibility with those morphisms (proof lines 3758-3775).

Construct the maps locally: on affine charts the existence of maps satisfying the degree zero and multiplicativity conditions follows from the syntomic local description and the local construction remark, and since the etale locus is the nonvanishing locus of $\delta(\NL_{Y/X})$, the maps become unique (and hence glue) whenever $\Omega_{X/\mathbf{Z}}$ is locally free and $\delta(\NL_{Y/X})$ has zero annihilator (proof lines 3777-3803).

Define the nice subcategory $\mathcal{C}_{nice}$ by those two conditions, obtain unique maps there, and note that compatibility with base change morphisms of $\mathcal{C}_{nice}$ follows from local existence plus uniqueness (proof lines 3805-3825).

Extend the construction along a morphism $b/a : Y'/X' \to Y/X$ with $Y/X$ in $\mathcal{C}_{nice}$: the base changed maps exist and are compatible, which is the object called $(b/a)^*c^p_{Y/X}$ (proof lines 3827-3835).

State and use the claim: for morphisms $Y_1/X_1 \leftarrow Y/X \to Y_2/X_2$ with both targets in $\mathcal{C}_{nice}$, the two base changes agree. Assuming the claim, glue the locally constructed maps along the universal families to get global maps on every object of $\mathcal{C}$ and check base change compatibility (proof lines 3837-3890).

Prove the claim: reduce to affine charts, lift the local isomorphisms along surjections of affine algebras, form the fibre product ring $A' = A'_1 \times_A A'_2 \to B'$ to obtain an auxiliary object $Y'/X'$ of $\mathcal{C}$, and compare the two base changes through the nice objects $Y'_i/X'_i$ and the universal family $Y_{n,d}/X_{n,d}$ pulled back around the square, which gives the agreement (proof lines 3892-3980).
proof_roadmap: Reformulation as a rule on the category $\mathcal{C}$ (proof lines 3758-3775).
Local construction and uniqueness after inverting the discriminant (proof lines 3777-3803).
The nice subcategory and base change within it (proof lines 3805-3835).
The claim, and the lemma deduced from it (proof lines 3837-3890).
Proof of the claim via affine fibre products and the universal family (proof lines 3892-3980).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs, and shows unique, the upstairs Garel maps on the differential forms of a locally quasi-finite syntomic morphism, compatible with the degree zero and multiplicativity conditions and with base change, with the composite against the pullback of differentials being multiplication by the discriminant (statement lines 3737-3751). The proof formalises the statement as a rule on a category of such morphisms, builds the maps locally and observes uniqueness after inverting the discriminant, solves the problem on the subcategory where the base differentials are free and the discriminant has zero annihilator, and then propagates the construction to all objects through the universal families, the crux being a claim that two base changes agree, proved by an affine fibre product manipulation. The five-stage structural argument is the substance, so the claim is H3.
